newsitem.title: USA: U.S. balloonist to try again to circle globe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. balloonist to try again to circle globe.

text.p: U.S. adventurer Steve Fossett will attempt again to be the first person to circumnavigate the globe in a hot-air balloon, nearly a year after his last effort ended in a Canadian crash-landing, his team announced on Thursday.

Fossett, a 52-year-old stock trader from Chicago, will brave 18 days of minus-50 degree Fahrenheit (-45 Celsius) exterior temperatures, unpredictable winds and passing airplanes to become the first balloonist to circle the globe non-stop, project manager Bo Kemper of Loyola University said.

His balloon, the $300,000 "Solo Spirit", will take off from Busch Stadium in St. Louis when global weather conditions are right -- 69 years after Charles Lindbergh flew his plane, "The Spirit of St. Louis", from New York to Paris in the first trans-Atlantic flight.

In a test-flight in September, Fossett set an unofficial balloon altitude record of 27,484 feet (8,376 metres). The planned trip will carry his unpressurized gondola to a height of between 18,000 feet to (5,486 metres) 24,000 feet (7,315 metres) at speeds up to 150 miles (240 km) per hour.
Fossett's previous flight in January ended a few hours after take-off when electrical malfunctions, heating problems and an East Coast storm forced a crash-landing in New Brunswick, Canada.
He has since set a world record for sailing solo across the Pacific in just over 20 days, to go with his first solo balloon crossing of the Pacific in 1995.
British entrepreneur Richard Branson has assembled his own team in a race to scale the balloonist's version of Mount Everest.
